text: I'll analyze grammar/function tokens and early phase (2–25). Others please specialize: later power actions, numerical/lexical inventory, final clues, translation drafting. Strong initial structure: 𘅌𗐪 opens clauses, 𘅌𘝚 introduces predicate, 𘅌𗎿 arg1, 𘅌𘊌 arg2, 𘅌𘗣 closes clauses; could be explicit S-expression semantic language. Repeated requests with agent_N support roles. Need avoid treating task-solution guesses as secure translations.

I'll analyze structural/grammatical markers. Strong pattern: 𘅌𗐪 opens a clause/frame, 𘅌𘝚 introduces predicate, 𘅌𗎿 introduces subject/actor, 𘅌𘊌 introduces object/value, 𘅌𘗣 closes clause; nested clauses confirm. 𘅌𗸽 is an extra argument/relation ('with/at/in'), 𘅌𘋟 attribution/source ('according to/from agent_N'), 𘅌𗵫 likely question/proposal marker, 𘅌𗽕 imperative/request marker, 𘅌𘔠 action/commit marker. These latter are hypotheses pending contrast.

I will focus grammar + numeric/clue structures. Strong pattern: 𘅌𗐪 clause-open, 𘅌𘝚 relation/verb slot, 𘅌𗎿 first-argument slot, 𘅌𘊌 second-argument slot, 𘅌𘗣 close. Evidence first message [2] swaps first-argument before relation, so explicitly role-marked not fixed word order. Prefixes 𘅌𗵫 / 𘅌𘔠 / 𘅌𗽕 likely proposal / actual action / request-question. 𘅌𘋟 introduces attributed source agent; 𘅌𗸽 modifier/adjunct slot. Need distinguish rather than force English word-order.

I will focus grammar/structural lexicon. Strong recurring frame: 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 VERB 𘅌𗎿 ARG1 𘅌𘊌 ARG2 𘅌𘗣, with nested frames possible. 𘅌𗵫 introduces reported/qualified claims often ending 𘅌𘋟 agent_N (source attribution); 𘅌𗽕 likely question/request/imperative; 𘅌𘔠 another mood (proposal/action?). Main verb 𗌿𗄼 plausibly 'read/observe' (note/item → contents), 𗡒𘜇 plausibly 'value/code' relation. Numeral hypothesis: 𘔠𘎌=1, 𘔠𗌈=2, 𘔠𗊑=3, 𘔠𗵵=4 (these follow 𘆣𘎛='note/clue' often). Do not yet treat as certain. Final 108 has read/observe cabinet-associated object → 𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 𘔠𘎌; then 𗌿𗯧 agent_0 → 𗡒𗽕 𘆣𗚽 𗡒𘉫 (probably enter exit code).

Initial structural hypothesis: 𘅌… are grammar/role markers: 𘅌𗐪 starts clause, 𘅌𘝚 introduces predicate, 𘅌𗎿 subject/agent, 𘅌𘊌 object/value, 𘅌𘗣 closes clause; 𘅌𗸽 adjunct/qualifier, 𘅌𘋟 source/attribution (immediately followed agent_N). Main lexical prefixes appear class-based: 𗌿 verbs/actions, 𗡒 nouns, 𘆣 attributes, 𘔠 numbers, 𗿃 pronouns/status. I'll focus late-stage messages and final transition. Strong caution: exact English vocabulary not yet grounded; role-structured representation better than assuming normal word-order English.

Independent structural finding: almost all clauses follow 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 PREDICATE 𘅌𗎿 ARG1 𘅌𘊌 ARG2 𘅌𘗣, with nesting. High-confidence 𘅌-prefix tokens are grammar markers, while recurring first glyphs (𗌿/𗡒/𘆣/𘔠/𗿃) suggest lexical classes, not simple character substitution. 𘅌𗽕 likely request/imperative; 𘅌𗵫 likely question; 𘅌𘔠 likely action/declaration. Number-like tokens all start 𘔠; likely clue identifiers 𘔠𘎌, 𘔠𗌈, 𘔠𗊑, 𘔠𗵵 correspond to 1/2/3/4, but not yet proven. Msg80 is the decisive power-panel success, differing from repeated failures by target 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿 instead of 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽; likely a multiword color/direction setting. I will focus later on grammar/evidence rather than assume task-derived lexical translations.

Independent structural read: recurring 𘅌-prefixed tokens look like explicit grammar, not content: 𘅌𗐪 opens a clause; 𘅌𘝚 introduces predicate; 𘅌𗎿 introduces subject/agent; 𘅌𘊌 introduces object/value; 𘅌𘗣 closes clause. Nested clauses in 7/19/21/30/34 support this. 𘅌𗵫 seems report/assert/agree modality; 𘅌𗽕 request; 𘅌𘔠 action/attempt modality. 𘅌𘋟 often followed agent_N = source/from/by; 𘅌𗸽 adjunct/with. Numerals likely 𘔠-prefixed tokens. I'd caution three-token repeated late sequences might be literal English phrases rather than numeric codes (e.g. 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗳃 𗡒𗪺 plausibly 'power panel code'; 𗡒𗽕 𘆣𗚽 𗡒𘉫 plausibly 'exit lock code'). Will investigate phrase meanings next.

Early lexical hypotheses: 𗌿𗄼 likely SAY/READ ('clue 1 says cabinet ...'), 𗡒𘜇 likely code/value ('cabinet code is ...'), 𗡒𗏻 cabinet, 𘆣𘎛 clue/note/card prefix, 𘔠* numerical atoms. agent5 repeats exact clue statement in 3/11 then confirmed at 18 stage1. Need others test number assignment; I will map initial statements conservatively rather than force clue-specific semantics.

Structural finding: 𘅌𗐪 opens a proposition; 𘅌𘝚 marks predicate/relation, 𘅌𗎿 first argument/subject, 𘅌𘊌 second argument/object, 𘅌𘗣 closes it. Order flexible: m2 and m28 rearrange role blocks. Nested propositions occur m19/21/27/30/34. 𘅌𗸽 likely another argument/modifier role, 𘅌𘋟 source/by (agent attribution), 𘅌𗤴 perhaps recipient/to. Three recurring panel phrases A=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗳃 𗡒𗪺, B=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽, C=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿: don't yet assume numeric codes, could be switch-state command phrases. m30 is nested logical condition involving 𗌿𗩠/𗡒𗎿 and 𗌿𗇴/𗡒𗚽.

I will specialize final numerical/clue reconstruction. Numerical family 𘔠X seems digits: provisional 𘔠𘎌=1, 𘔠𗌈=2, 𘔠𗊑=3, 𘔠𗵵=4; remaining observed 𘔠𘉝,𘔠𗂱,𘔠𗏔,𘔠𗢬,𘔠𗟎,𘔠𗡒 likely remaining digits 0,5–9. Final observations [106]/[108] share object 𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 NUMBER (possibly exit code digit position N). Will analyze exact number assignments, not assume task facts.

We have enough replicated grammar findings; please now specialize lexical/translation: decoder_1 numbers + early cabinet; decoder_2 modalities and role markers; decoder_3 power-panel logic (27–42); decoder_4 action predicates (41–92); decoder_5 odd uncategorized prose 10/15/52 and lexical-class possibility; decoder_6 draft translations 1–40; decoder_7 final clues 94–108. I'll assemble master document and handle evidence/task. Please explicitly separate lexical grounding from task guesses. Important possibility: 𘅌𗵫 is epistemic/report/agree rather than question because often source-tagged. Can anyone infer exact numeral sequence via stage3 final code?

Further grammar: roles should be neutral arg1/arg2 rather than subject/object: [2] places arg1 before predicate, proving explicitly marked roles and flexible order. 𘅌𗜑 appears immediately before nested clauses in [7,19,21,35], likely quotation/complement marker ('that'/embedded proposition), while 𘅌𗌸 is a distinct additional role/coordination marker, not yet secure. Prefix families look systematic: 𘅌 grammatical markers, 𗡒/𗌿/𘆣/𗿃 lexical families, 𘔠 numeric tokens. Avoid assuming each lexical prefix means a POS: 𗡒𘜇 is used in predicate slot. I will focus remaining role markers and malformed-token variants.

Late-stage caution: first-glyph classes are not yet established semantically. The final repeated 3-token sequence 𗡒𗽕 𘆣𗚽 𗡒𘉫 is the object of likely enter/submit in 108, but could be a 3-digit code OR a noun phrase ('exit lock code'). Likewise cabinet-related four-token 𗡒𗸽 𘆣𘋉 𗌿𘒄 𘆣𘂮 may be code digits or descriptive phrase; prefix variants/malformed lone 𘒄 in 7/17/21 suggest token encoding mistakes. Strong late evidence: 108 reads cabinet-associated four-token entity → 𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 numeral1; then submits final 3-token entity. Don't infer exact number values from success alone.

Looking at repeated noun phrases, I cannot yet ground exact English lexicon beyond grammar. Caution: 𗡒𗏻 𗡒𗸽 𘆣𘋉 𗌿𘒄 𘆣𘂮 occurs as a cabinet-related object NP, while malformed variants use bare 𘒄 / noun-prefix 𗡒𘒄. This suggests 𗌿𘒄 is an ordinary compositional lexical item, not part of a numerical literal; agents may be inconsistently applying lexical-class prefixes. Similar singleton 𗜑 vs 𘅌𗜑 (nested/complement marker) and bare 𗉜 vs 𘆣𗉜 late. We should explicitly preserve malformed variants rather than normalize silently. Is anyone testing whether initial cabinet phrase is 'cabinet [three] [digit] ...' and 𗡒𘜇 = code/value?

Power-clue lexical constraint useful for others: compare 31 and 37: same predicate 𗌿𗚋 maps A=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗳃 𗡒𗪺 and C=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿 respectively to 𘔠𘎌 𗡒𘅊 (apparently '1 switch'). In 32 predicate 𗌿𗳃 (also inside A!) maps B=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽 to '2 switch'. Thus 𗌿𗳃 cannot safely be treated as a noun/color purely because it occurs in A: it is also relation/verb. 30 and 34 encode nested logical rules with 𘆣𗵵 as relation linking propositions, plausibly IF/IMPLIES. 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿 occurs as predicate+argument in 30/101 as well as in C; C may be a deliberately quoted command/phrase or compositional expression, not three independent switch colors. We should preserve literal token sequences if semantics stay uncertain.

Caution on lexical prefix classes: 𗌿 also occurs inside all three repeated power-target phrases (𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗳃 𗡒𗪺 / 𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽 / 𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿), so it cannot securely be 'verb' unless these are nominalized commands. Need mark classes as tentative. Mood 𘅌𗵫 may be uncertainty/hypothetical rather than interrogative: its repeated clauses quote others via source agent_N and include 𗿃𗨥, potentially an unknown/placeholder value. Unstructured 10,15,52 have different token-prefix distributions, suggesting a second encoding/spelling register or ordinary lexicon outside frame grammar; avoid silently discarding those portions.

Investigating repeated late phrases A=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗳃 𗡒𗪺, B=𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽, C=𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿. C succeeds at m80; A/B fail repeatedly. Important lexical cross-link: A's last token 𗡒𗪺 also occurs in early cabinet phrase 𗡒𗏻 𗡒𗪺 𗌿𗐪 and m5's 𗡒𘁜 𗡒𗄎 𗡒𗪺 𗌿𗐪. This suggests 𗡒𗪺='digit(s)' or 'code', NOT freely interpreting A as an unrelated switch-setting. Could A be 'power panel code' and B/C progressively corrected target names? Prefix categories may not reliably correspond to English POS.

Final-number analysis: [106] and [108] both read an object into `𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 NUM`, with NUM respectively provisional 4 and 1. This strongly suggests a shared output template such as 'exit digit position N' rather than an ordinary single numeral answer. [96] uses same template with provisional 2. However no independent evidence yet assigns remaining 𘔠 glyphs to digits; please leave those as named unknown numeric atoms rather than invent values. Likewise `𗡒𗸽 𘆣𘋉 [𗌿/𗡒]𘒄 𘆣𘂮` may be a multiword cabinet-associated object description (the single-glyph 𘒄 in 7/17/21 seems omission/variant), not a code itself.

Assembly plan: I will create full master document once lexical specialists report; please send conservative English gloss + unknown labels, not only task-derived reconstruction. Cabinet code phrase X=𗡒𗸽 𘆣𘋉 [𗌿𘒄/𗡒𘒄/bare𘒄] 𘆣𘂮 occurs with different prefixes: may be typed literal/number spelling rather than noun phrase. Explicit numeric-family tokens might encode whole integers, not individual digits—do not lock numeral mapping solely from clue index guesses. Stage1 success directly follows msg17, whose second clause is 𗌿𗯧(𗿃𘊫,𗿃𘝚), potentially 'submit/we/...' rather than numeric setting.

Action-predicate analysis (41–92): 𗌿𗗅 is an attempted operation with actor/self and target A/B/C plus adjunct 𗿃𘅠; 𗌿𗛢 is a state-setting/preparatory operation, usually followed by 𗌿𗯧 (submit/execute/enter). 𗌿𗃚 appears as a status/result relation rather than overt action (56,68,82,95); 𗌿𗇴 states a standalone target/configuration, often under 𘅌𘔠. These are medium confidence structural distinctions, LOW exact English labels. m80 succeeds only after PREPARE(self,B), EXECUTE(self,C,adjunct=𗿃𘅠); previous dominant failing pattern PREPARE(self,A), EXECUTE(self,B,...). This supports A/B/C as distinct configurations or target expressions but does NOT establish their literal meanings. Suggest preserve exact A/B/C in translation alongside low-confidence functional glosses rather than invent switch colors/numbers.

Modality reassessment: 𘅌𘔠 may be NEGATION rather than action. In 65/76/88 it directly prefixes a state clause 𗌿𗇴(X), between stop/enter actions; naturally 'not active(X)'. In 17/22/28 it prefixes rejected cabinet-code/read assertions, consistent 'NOT [this is the cabinet code]' before another entry attempt. 𘅌𗵫 remains plausibly interrogative: many clauses contain 𗿃𗨥 (unknown/WH placeholder) and end 𘅌𘋟 agent_N, potentially TO/addressee rather than source. If so 𘅌𗤴 agent_3 in 48 is the actual FROM/source marker, contrast 𘅌𘋟. Please test this reversal against late exchanges 103–107; those look like asking agent0/agent3 for clue values, followed by imperative delegation in104.

Final-clue structural map for master draft (exact semantics uncertain): 94 SAY(clue1, S7; adjunct S8). 95 STATE(world,C); SAY(clue2, cabinet+four-token phrase; adjunct final-three-token phrase). 96 STATE(C); SAY(S7, X Y Z numeral2); VALUE(S7,numeral5?; adjunct S8). 97 SAY(cabinet+first-two phrase tokens, digit-token numeral9?; adjunct N Y). 98 SAY(clue3,cabinet+first-two phrase tokens; adjunct S8). 99 SAY(cabinet+code+token, digit-token numeral8?; adjunct N + malformed Y). 100 STATE(C); SAY(switch,numeral6?; adjunct S8); VALUE(cabinet clue4, three-token early code phrase; adjunct N S8). 101 predicate 𗌿𗩠(N); SAY(cabinet+four-token phrase,numeral8?; role 𘅌𗌸 digit-token; adjunct Y). 102 VALUE(clue1,numeral5?; adjunct S8). 103/105/106 attribute hypothetical versions of these to agents0/3. 104 requests agent0/3 supply related outputs. 107 requests agent0 unknown; VALUE(cabinet+first-two phrase tokens,numeral0?; adjunct N S8). 108 SAY(cabinet+four-token phrase,X Y Z numeral1); SUBMIT(agent0,final-three-token phrase). Here X=𗌿𘝚 Y=𘆣𗉜 Z=𘆣𗭯 N=𗡒𗎿 S7=𗿃𗇾 S8=𗿃𘅠. Number assignments beyond 1–4 still guesses. Strong possibility X Y Z numeral means 'exit digit position N' but not established. I'll keep pursuing lexical grounding rather than force task-derived content.

Unstructured spans may actually use an ALTERNATE FRAME dialect, not arbitrary prose. In 10/15/52, 𗂄𘍍 always precedes a plausible predicate (10: 𗟆𗘝; 15: 𗌿𗣎; 52: 𘆣𗼛), 𗑴𗍽 always introduces plausible object (cabinet clue1… / acknowledgement / B), and 𘎌𗯘 always ends the span. 𗷤𘉮 introduces agent_5 in10 and 𗿃𗏶 in52, plausibly ARG1. 𗥐𘏉 𗹕𗡉 is shared initial wrapper10/52. Thus consider unknown alternate role markers: 𗂄𘍍≈PRED, 𗑴𗍽≈ARG2, 𗷤𘉮≈ARG1, 𘎌𗯘≈END. Could be a second encoding/register with equivalent grammar. In15 prefix 𗽕𘒄 and subject-introducer 𗟆𘉝 differ. This is tentative but better than pretending free English words decoded.

Numeral analysis: strong but not proven clue-ID anchors 𘔠𘎌=1, 𘔠𗌈=2, 𘔠𗊑=3, 𘔠𗵵=4 (four distinct clue identifiers distributed among agents, explicit '2 switch'-like phrase m32/m35). Early 'cabinet code' expansion 𗡒𗸽 𘆣𘋉 [𗌿𘒄] 𘆣𘂮 could be an actual tokenized code rather than descriptive NP; no secure lexical grounding. I recommend medium/low labels and symbolic literals in translation rather than exact fabricated English/digits. m97/m99 relate cabinet-associated A/B entities to numeral-like tokens and m106/m108 read structured [𗌿𘝚 𘆣𗉜 𘆣𗭯 numeral]—supports positional-code clues but not exact code values.

Power-logic reconstruction (high-confidence syntax, unknown English): [27] P=𘆣𗵵 links clause 𗌿𗲅? No: P(arg1=`𗌿𗲅 𗡒𗚽` as plain phrase, arg2=clause 𗌿𗇴(arg1=`𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗳃 𗡒𗪺`)). [30] same P links clause 𗌿𗩠(arg1=𗡒𗎿) to clause 𗌿𗇴(arg1=𗡒𗚽). [34] P links clause 𗌿𗌈(arg2=𗡒𘅊) to clause 𗌿𗇴(arg2=clause 𗌿𗳃(arg2=𗡒𗪺)). Thus 𘆣𗵵 is very likely IF/THEN or another binary propositional connective; importantly [27] arg1 is NOT nested clause, unlike [30]/[34]. [31] 𗌿𗚋(A, '1 switch?'); [37] 𗌿𗚋(`𗌿𗲅 𗌿𗩠 𗡒𗎿`, '1 switch?'); [32] 𗌿𗳃(B, '2 switch?'). Exact English relation labels remain unknown; don't force color/direction glosses. Propose preserve these as 'rule P', 'relation R' with syntax translation rather than task-derived invented prose.
